task.name: A document that policy requires a semantic review for is left unevaluated until an operator runs the evaluator by hand, so the gate withholds admission for work nothing has been scheduled to do
task.story_text:
Semantic readiness policy marks a typed document `required` once it reaches implementation
readiness, and a document with no evaluation record for its current revision is withheld
from admission. Nothing schedules that evaluation. The evaluator runs only when an operator
invokes it for one issue at a time, so the gate withholds work on the absence of a step no
part of the system has been asked to perform.

The effect is a state the intake contract does not intend: the document is structurally
runnable, policy declares a review necessary, and the only path forward is a keystroke per
issue. The milestone's own goal is capture → shaped → groomed → ready without operator
keystrokes, and this is the one transition that still demands them.

This is the sixth producer of the shape-gate router (#1450). The other five — diagnose,
groom, and their supporting slices — are filed. The semantic evaluator was not among them
because it did not exist when that epic was written.

Automatic invocation is a change to *what runs*, not to *what a result means*. A raised
finding still withholds admission until an operator ratifies it, and nothing here records a
ratification on the operator's behalf. Whether a clean evaluation can clear a document
without a per-issue operator decision is a separate question, governed by ADR-0009 clause 6,
and is deliberately not decided here.

## Acceptance criteria

- A document that policy marks as requiring a semantic review, and that has no evaluation
  record for its current revision, has one performed without an operator command. A document
  policy marks as not requiring one has no evaluation performed for it, and neither the
  presence nor absence of a record changes its admission.

- An evaluation is bound to the exact revision that occasioned it. A document whose revision
  changes does not carry a prior evaluation forward; the new revision reports as unevaluated
  until an evaluation runs against it.

- Automatic invocation changes only whether an evaluation happens. A raised finding withholds
  admission until an operator ratification is recorded against that revision, exactly as it
  does when the evaluator is invoked by hand, and no automatic path records a ratification.

- An evaluation that fails, times out, is refused, or cannot be attempted at all leaves the
  document reporting the failure and unevaluated. No failure mode leaves a document reading
  as evaluated-clean, and an unrecognised outcome is treated as a failure rather than mapped
  onto a known result.

- Invocation is bounded by the evidence it produces: a document is evaluated at most once per
  revision per prompt contract version, and a transition that recurs against an unchanged
  revision reuses the existing record rather than spending again.

- Operator invocation continues to work for any document, including one policy does not
  require a review for, and records its result on the same terms as an automatic one.

## Example

An enhancement is groomed until the structural gate returns runnable, which makes policy
require a semantic review of it. Today the ready queue withholds it as
`semantic_review_not_ratified` and stops; the operator discovers this by finding the issue
missing from the queue, then runs the evaluator and the ratification by hand.

With this in place, reaching that state performs the evaluation against that revision and
records it. Two outcomes follow:

```
no findings   → the record exists; admission still awaits the operator's ratification,
                which is one decision rather than two commands
findings      → the concerns are on record for that revision, and admission is withheld
                until the operator accepts or rejects them — unchanged from today
```

A subsequent edit to the body makes the recorded evaluation inapplicable, and the new
revision is evaluated in turn rather than inheriting the old result. An evaluation that
fails to parse leaves the document unevaluated with the failure recorded, and the document
is not admitted on the strength of a failure.

handoff.summary: No new work this invocation: the story was already implemented on feat/issue-2907 across three commits (feature plus two review iterations), which have since been rebased onto current main. I verified the tree is clean, the implementation is intact after the rebase (semantic_auto.py present with ensure_semantic_evaluation, semantic_issue_entry_admission, semantic_dispatch_withholding and the tri-state scheduling lock), and re-ran make dev-check: 11109 passed, with 17 failures that are all pre-existing sandbox PermissionErrors in test_sprint_lock.py and test_cut_rc_isolation.py (multiprocessing semaphores and mkstemp), unchanged in count and identity by this branch. The implementation adds eval/semantic_auto.py, a total helper that derives semantic readiness and, only for a policy-required revision with no attempt on record, invokes the existing evaluator against the exact revision the caller already fetched (fed through review_issue_semantically's gh_issue_view seam so no re-fetch can race an edit), serialized by a non-blocking per-revision flock. Scheduling is reached from query-mode gate admission via apply_shape_gate's semantic_readiness seam, from query-mode re-admission of issues entry remediation puts back after the gate's pass, and from manifest issue entries; ready_queue stays read-only because a status command must not spend, and --dry-run is exempt from the dispatch check because it makes no admission decision to check against. Storage gained latest_attempt_for_revision (revision + contract keyed, sees failures) used only by the automatic path, leaving latest_record_for_identity's manual-path cache semantics untouched, and baseline provenance so an automatically frozen empty baseline does not foreclose an operator's real one. TaskStory carries the revision identity of the fetch that built it so the dispatch check validates the exact payload a dev agent receives without a second gh call.

story_deviations: Automatic scheduling is stricter than AC5's literal bound: it invokes only when the revision has no successful record under ANY prompt contract version, not merely none under the active one. derive_semantic_readiness prefers any successful record for the digest before considering failures, so scheduling a new contract over a ratified older success would let the fresh failure be masked by the stale success — the opposite of the fail-closed criterion. Staying inside AC5's 'at most once' bound avoids that without changing what admission consumes.

FrozenSemanticBaseline gained a provenance field (human/automatic), and freeze_baseline lets a human freeze supersede an automatically frozen EMPTY baseline. Not named in an AC, but without it the automatic path's placeholder would permanently foreclose an operator's real baseline for that revision and would read as a zero-defect human baseline in golden-set calibration. Human baselines remain immutable.

TaskStory gained source_revision_digest / source_revision_type, populated by GitHubIssueSource.fetch over the raw body. Chosen over a re-fetch at dispatch time because it costs no gh call and validates exactly the payload the dev agent receives; file stories leave both None and are never withheld by the check.

tests/conftest.py's existing _neutral_semantic_readiness_overlay fixture neutralizes the two further seams this story adds (semantic_dispatch_withholding, semantic_issue_entry_admission), on the same grounds as the three it already covered: no fixture in the suite records a ratified review, so leaving them live would withhold every well-shaped issue in tests that are not about semantic readiness.

Semantic-admission spend is disclosed, not metered. The evaluator runs before the sprint's cost ledger exists, so its cost cannot be advanced through SprintExecutionState.cost; the sprint CONVENTIONS give the cap three owners and this is not one of them. _disclose_semantic_admission_spend prints the evaluation count and recorded cost and states plainly that it is outside --budget.
deferred_items: Metering semantic-admission spend against --budget. The records already carry cost_usd; carrying it into the sprint's carried-spend restoration is a change to the cap mechanism and belongs to its owner (budget_runtime.py). Spend is disclosed on stderr in the meantime.

ready_queue.py remains read-only by design (a status command must not spend), so `forge status --ready` shows a required-unevaluated issue as withheld until a sprint or manifest run schedules the evaluation. Status-time scheduling would be a separate story.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 explicitly guards automatic invocation by (input_digest, model_id, prompt_contract_version), using or extending SemanticReviewStore.latest_record_for_identity() in src/theforge/eval/semantic_storage.py. The acceptance criterion permits at most one automatic evaluation per revision and prompt-contract version, irrespective of model. Changing the configured profile/model would therefore spend again for the same revision and contract.
  Suggestion: Give the automatic path a lookup keyed only by issue/revision and prompt-contract version, including successful and failed attempts. Keep the existing model-specific cache behavior for manual evaluation if required.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 says to leave latest_successful_record admission semantics unchanged and re-derive readiness after the attempt. derive_semantic_readiness() in src/theforge/eval/semantic_readiness.py selects any successful record for the digest before considering failures, without prompt-contract identity. If an older contract succeeded and was ratified but the newly scheduled contract fails, readiness still returns reviewed_ready; the new failure is masked, contradicting the fail-closed criterion.
  Suggestion: Make readiness select the attempt applicable to the active automatic prompt contract, or otherwise ensure the newest applicable failed attempt takes precedence over stale success. Add a test with a ratified v1 success followed by a v2 failure.
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Step 1 proposes a lookup-then-invoke sequence, but SemanticReviewStore uses unlocked JSONL reads/appends. Concurrent query and manifest admissions can both observe no attempt and invoke the evaluator, so the stated at-most-once guarantee is not atomic.
  Suggestion: Serialize automatic scheduling with a per-identity lock or durable reservation covering the attempt check through evidence persistence, and test two concurrent scheduling calls.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 2 (status surfaces and agent spend) is carried, not retired: Step 5 states the ready_queue outcome as an unresolved fork ('If ready_queue is changed to invoke the helper directly … otherwise leave it read-only'). The spec's own example frames the ready queue as where the operator discovers the withholding, so leaving it read-only means the evaluation is only scheduled when an operator starts a sprint or manifest run.
  Suggestion: Decide it in the plan rather than at implementation: keep ready_queue.py read-only (a status command must not spend), and make Step 5 comment/assertion work only — assert in tests that listing a required-unevaluated issue invokes no agent runner. If reviewers later want status-time scheduling, that is a separate story, not an in-flight fork.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Risk 3's mitigation ('add or adjust a SemanticReviewStore lookup so automatic scheduling can see both successful and failed attempts') can silently change the manual path. latest_record_for_identity (semantic_storage.py:343-359) deliberately filters to STATUS_FINDINGS/STATUS_NO_FINDINGS; widening it to include STATUS_EVALUATION_FAILED would make forge review-semantic return a cache hit on a prior failure instead of retrying, which is a behaviour change to the operator command Step 6 promises to leave alone.
  Suggestion: Add a new method (e.g. latest_attempt_for_identity) used only by the automatic helper and leave latest_record_for_identity untouched; add a test that a failed record still lets the manual command re-invoke the agent.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] The shape-gate seam is fail-open: any exception from derive_readiness is logged and readiness is set to None (shape_gate.py:574-578), after which the issue is appended to runnable. If the new automatic helper lets an exception escape — agent-launch wrapper error, store write failure, or freeze_baseline's ValueError when an existing baseline's defect_ids differ (semantic_storage.py:402-410) — a policy-required document is admitted with no semantic state at all, which is exactly the 'reads as clean on a failure' outcome AC4 forbids.
  Suggestion: Make the helper total: catch everything internally, append a STATUS_EVALUATION_FAILED record where a digest is computable, and always return a derived SemanticReadiness (STATE_EVALUATION_FAILED withholds via reason_code SEMANTIC_EVALUATION_FAILED_CODE). Add a test that an agent_runner raising leaves the issue skipped, not runnable.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 1's baseline handling (Risk 1's mitigation) is correct only if the helper passes baseline_defect_ids=None when a baseline already exists. Passing () unconditionally would hit freeze_baseline's 'already frozen and cannot be changed' ValueError for any digest whose baseline carries non-empty defect_ids (semantic_runner.py:281-287 → semantic_storage.py:402-410).
  Suggestion: Have the helper call store.frozen_baseline(digest) first and pass () only when it returns None; cover with the 'existing baselines are preserved' test the plan already promises.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-fable-cli] The automatic empty-baseline freeze (Step 1) permanently forecloses a later human baseline for that digest: freeze_baseline (semantic_storage.py:392-411) raises ValueError on any attempt to change a frozen baseline, so once the automatic path freezes an empty one, an operator can never record real baseline defect ids for that revision, and golden-set calibration in semantic_report.py:245-303 will count that digest as a zero-defect human baseline. The plan makes the freeze decision correctly for admission purposes but doesn't note this calibration side effect.
  Suggestion: Consider marking automatically-frozen baselines distinguishably (e.g. a provenance field or reserved issue_ref convention) or documenting in the Step 1 comment that auto-frozen empty baselines are excluded from calibration claims; at minimum the dev agent should ensure the ValueError path from a later differing manual --baseline-defect-id freeze produces an intelligible operator message.
- [P2] [anthropic-fable-cli] Step 5 leaves ready_queue's behavior as an either/or ('if ready_queue is changed... otherwise leave it read-only'), deferring the choice to the dev agent. The plan's own risk 2 says status surfaces should not spend; the safe branch is clearly the intended one but the step doesn't commit to it.
  Suggestion: Implement the read-only branch: leave ready_queue as a reporter of records produced by the sprint/manifest admission paths and update its comments, per the risk 2 mitigation's stated preference.
- [P2] [anthropic-fable-cli] Step 3's closure must synthesize a gh_issue_view-compatible CompletedProcess from the gate's already-fetched title/body/labels to guarantee the evaluated revision matches the withheld one, since review_issue_semantically (semantic_runner.py:255-259) always re-fetches through that callable; the plan states the intent but not the mechanism.
  Suggestion: Have the closure pass a gh_issue_view stub returning the gate's fetched detail as JSON (or refactor a load-bypassing entry point in the helper) rather than letting a second live gh fetch race a concurrent edit.

soft: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions
Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.
Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports
Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it
Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.
